deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a set of German notes on ancient Greek, specifically Athenian, history. It continues the previous page, which covers the archons, Draco and the Solonian property classes, and leads into the next page on the Ionian revolt and Greek colonies. It reads like notes from a university history lecture, possibly in the style of Heeren's Göttingen lectures. The hand and content give no sign that this is Gauss's own mathematical work. It may be a student's or family member's notebook filed in the bundle.

Content, step by step:
(1) After Solon's reform the (nine) archons remain, and a council of 400 is set beside them.
(2) Solon leaves Athens and new unrest follows. The oppressed party seeks redress against the oppressors. Pisistratus leads the popular party and Megacles the other.
(3) Pisistratus wins and seizes supreme power some years after Solon's legislation, but leaves the Solonian constitution in place. He is driven out twice and returns each time. He is first expelled in 560, a second time in 55[?], and retakes power by force in 538, marching against Athens at the head of his supporters. He holds power until his death, written as 528/526.
(4) His sons Hipparchus and Hippias rule jointly until 514.
(5) Harmodius and Aristogiton conspire against them. The plot only half succeeds: Hipparchus is murdered and Hippias survives.
(6) The Alcmaeonids, who had fled to Macedonia, gather the malcontents from Athens and retake the city in 510. Hippias flees to the Persian king Darius.
(7) Encouraged by their freedom, the Athenians take part around 500 in the revolt of the Asiatic Greeks, which the next page continues with the burning of Sardis.
errors: Historical, not mathematical. The dates follow an older chronology that differs from modern ones. Modern dating: Solon's archonship 594/3; Pisistratus's first tyranny 561/0; first expulsion c. 556; second exile c. 555; return after the Battle of Pallene c. 546; death 528/7; Hipparchus murdered 514; Hippias expelled 510; Ionian revolt 499, Sardis burned 498.

'21 Jahre nach Solons Gesetzgebung' does not fit the page's own dates. With Solon's archonship at 592 and Pisistratus in power by 560, the gap is about 32 years. The digit is probably a misreading, or the writer slipped.
The sequence '560 ... erstemal vertrieben' is confused. 560 is conventionally the year Pisistratus first seized power, not the year of his first expulsion.

results.what: Lecture notes on Athenian political history from Solon to the Ionian revolt (Pisistratids, Harmodius and Aristogiton, the Alcmaeonids)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th/19th-century university history curriculum (e.g. A. H. L. Heeren at Göttingen)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely historical lecture notes with no mathematical content. It is probably not even Gauss's own composition.

checkable.asserts: The interval between Solon's archonship (592, as given on the previous page) and Pisistratus's tyranny (560) is 32 years, not 21. This makes the '21 Jahre' reading or statement doubtful.
Hippias ruled alone for 4 years between Hipparchus's murder (514) and his own expulsion (510).

transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Die 4 Archonten' should almost certainly read 'Die 9 Archonten'. The digit looks like a 9, and Athens had nine archons.
Line 4: 'zu treiben' is more plausibly 'zu rächen' (to take revenge on the oppressing party).
The year of Pisistratus's death read as '† 526' may be '† 528' in the image, which matches the conventional date of 528/7.

'Zur Ausführung ihres Komplots wählten[?]' should be checked against the image, which appears to read '... ihres Komplots wählten sie ...'. The following lines are badly garbled in the machine transcription.
'an ihrer[?] Spitze gegen seine Gegner[?] der gegen Athen marschirten' probably reads '... an ihrer Spitze gegen seine Gegner, die gegen Athen marschirten'.
